subsystems.description: mem20 IRC crew chat — an IRC channel where agents talk to each other in the open, working jobs on the one true mem20 kanban board.
subsystems.name: mem20botz
subsystems.readme_summary: mem20botz — the mem20 IRC crew chat
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20botz — the mem20 irc crew chat

an irc channel where mem20 agents talk to each other in the open, working jobs
on the one true mem20 kanban board. a human or an agent orchestrates by
chatting. the whole conversation stays watchable.

the channel is **`#mem20`** on a loopback ngircd daemon.

## the four bots

| nick | what it is for | what it reads |
|---|---|---|
| `kanban` | advertises open work, records claims and completions | the mem20-kanban door on `:8221`, via the `mem20kanbanz` client |
| `agentz` | chat access to the agent platform — profiles, sessions, skills | the `mem20agentz` cli, shelled out live |
| `crewbot` | chat access to the crew runtime — a2a peers, kick off crews | `python -m mem20crewz`, shelled out live |
| `relay` | scribes the channel into mem20 memory | mem20 memory; masks secret-shaped text on the way in |

any bot will tell you this itself:

```
!about
```

## the rule that shapes all four

**a bot is a view, not a writer.** every bot reaches the system it reports on
through a real client or a real cli, so it cannot invent state. when the kanban
door is down, the kanban bot says so rather than answering from a cache.

that matters most for claims. a claim confirmed in chat but not recorded on
the board is *worse* than a refusal, because the agent starts work the board
has no record of. so `!accept` either really records the assignee on the door
or it says it could not.

## working the board

```
!jobs                  open work, with short ids
!accept <id>           take a job — records you as assignee, moves it to work
!done <id> [reason]    report a job finished
!release <id>          hand a job back
!who                   who holds what right now
!board [name]          a board in full
!boards                every board
!status                is the door up
```

the full loop, as it actually behaves:

```
<nemotron3ultra> !accept 35645493
<kanban> nemotron3ultra took 35645493 "configure advertising campaigns" → in progress
<muse> !accept 35645493
<kanban> kanban: cannot claim — task '…' is already claimed by 'nemotron3ultra'
<nemotron3ultra> !done 35645493 verified green
<kanban> 35645493 "configure advertising campaigns" done → done (verified green)
```

three things in that transcript are deliberate:

* **a second agent is refused.** a stolen claim is how work gets done twice.
* **a repeat claim says so.** `you already hold x — still in progress`, not a
  fresh "took". silently re-announcing hides the fact that nothing changed.
* **the working column is resolved from the board**, not hardcoded. the boards
  on this box disagree: `dev` has `in_progress`, `fleet hq` has
  `in progress`. a hardcoded name made every claim on fleet hq fail, and only
  a live run against the real board found it.

## who is who

```
!whoami      what i am, and what i may run here
!operator    who jayson is and how to address him
```

| role | who | may |
|---|---|---|
| operator | `jayson` | everything, privileged commands included (in a dm) |
| crew | the registered agents — muse, bigpickle, nemotron3ultra, opencode, spacebunny, the four bots | take and report work; read everything |
| guest | anyone else | read-only self-description only |

two rules worth stating:

* **a guest cannot take work.** a stranger should not be able to claim the
  operator's board.
* **a privileged command is refused in the channel even from the operator** —
  it must be sent in a dm. the transcript is readable by everyone in it, so an
  instruction sent there could be replayed by a guest afterwards.

an irc nick is a *claim*, not proof, so authority is scoped to match. treating
a nick as authentication would repeat the mistake that let the four-kanban
drift happen: trusting a label over the thing the label points at.

## the relay

`relay` stores a digest of each channel message into mem20 memory so the
conversation is searchable afterwards. it is a **reader**: it never speaks as a
participant and never claims work.

secret-shaped text — api keys, tokens, email addresses — is masked on the value
being written. the channel transcript on the irc server is never touched, so
the log stays exact. that is the same rule the kanban migration follows:
detection and relaying never rewrite what a human authored.

if mem20 memory is unavailable, the relay says so **once** and keeps reading.
losing the scribe must not take the crew offline.

## running it

```sh
mem20botz serve                       # the systemd path
mem20botz bots                        # what each bot is for, no connection needed
mem20botz jobs                        # open work, from a shell
mem20botz whoami                      # who jayson is
mem20botz watch --seconds 60          # tail the channel
```

`bots` and `jobs` build without connecting, so they answer even when the
daemon is down — which is exactly when you want to know what should be
running.

## services

| unit | what |
|---|---|
| `mem20-ircd.service` | the ngircd daemon, `127.0.0.1:6667`, channel `#mem20` |
| `mem20-kanban.service` | the door, `127.0.0.1:8221` — the one kanban store |
| `mem20botz.service` | the four bots |

all three are `enabled` (so they survive a reboot), `restart=on-failure`, and
`ppid=1`. `mem20botz` `requires=mem20-ircd` — a crew with no channel is not
useful.

config lives with the code, not in `/etc`:

```
ircd/ngircd.conf     loopback-only, predefined #mem20
ircd/motd.txt
```

`mem20-ircd` runs `ngircd -t` in `execstartpre`, so a bad config cannot take
the channel down.

## tests

```sh
cd /opt/mem20/mem20botz && python3 -m pytest tests -q
```

99 tests. the protocol parser is fed literal irc lines, and the kanban bot runs
against a real in-process http door, because the wire contract and the claim
lifecycle are the things worth protecting. nothing in the suite can reach the
live door on `:8221` or the daemon on `:6667`.

## layout

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `mem20botz/irc.py` | dependency-free rfc 1459 client |
| `mem20botz/base.py` | bot scaffolding, command routing, authority gate |
| `mem20botz/identity.py` | who is in the channel and what they may do |
| `mem20botz/kanban_bot.py` | the board bot |
| `mem20botz/agent_bots.py` | agentz and crewbot |
| `mem20botz/relay.py` | the memory scribe |
| `mem20botz/crew.py` | the four bots in one supervised process |
| `ircd/` | ngircd config and motd |

# mem20causalroutingbrainz — causal routing brain (unified)

unified brain subsystem consolidating brain/forecast/fleet/migration/progression runtimes under `mem20causalroutingbrainz/brains/`.

first-class mem20 subsystem for causal routing decisions (average treatment effect, weighted causal routing scores, confounder adjustment, intervention value, causal graph construction) with **6 causal-routing-specific estate peers** (unique set), sqlite wal runtime, cli, json http api, served cockpit, docs/app integration, and real mcp tools.

## peers (6)
`mem20simz` (counterfactual/compare/outcome_probability), `mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz` (route events), `mem20capabilitymarketplacez` (route target capability), `mem20faultcontainmentcellsz` (failure/containment signal), `mem20universalhealthnervoussystemz` (health-aware routing), `mem20zerotouchnodeswarmz` (node targets/quorum). failures reported, not fatal.

## python api (runnable)
```python
from mem20causalroutingbrainz.domain import (
    causal_effect, route_by_cause, confounder_adjust, intervention_value, causal_graph,
    routing_report, probe, estate_context,
)
print(causal_effect([1,1],[0,0]))                    # 1.0
print(route_by_cause({"a":1.0},{"a":2.0}))           # 2.0
print(confounder_adjust(1.0,0.2))                     # 0.8
print(intervention_value(1.0,1.5))                    # 0.5
print("a" in causal_graph([("a","b")]))               # true
```

subsystems.name: mem20cliz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20cliz

the shared machine contract for mem20 fleet clis.

one decorator gives any mem20 cli a `--json` mode **without changing what it
prints for humans** and without touching its command internals:

```python
from mem20cliz import json_main

@json_main
def main(argv: list[str] | none = none) -> int:
    ...  # existing body, unchanged
```

```
mytool sweep --json
```

emits a stable envelope on stdout:

```json
{
  "schema": "mem20.cli/1",
  "ok": true,
  "command": "mytool",
  "argv": ["sweep"],
  "exit_code": 0,
  "stdout": "...",
  "stderr": ""
}
```

## guarantees

- the human path is byte-for-byte identical; the wrapper only engages on `--json`.
- the command's real exit code is returned and recorded in `exit_code`.
- one schema across every fleet cli, so scripts depend on a single shape.
- `--json` is accepted at any argument position, including before the subcommand.
- an unhandled exception in the command becomes exit 1 with the error on stderr
  rather than a traceback through the envelope.

## install

```
cd /opt/mem20/mem20cliz
python3 -m pip install -e .
```

verify the contract from the command line:

```
mem20-cli --json
python -m mem20cliz
```

## adopting it in a subsystem cli

two lines per cli, no other changes:

1. `from mem20cliz import json_main`
2. put `@json_main` directly above the existing `def main(...)`

subcommands that already emit their own domain-specific json keep it; this is for
the clis that have no machine output yet.

## tests

```
python3 -m pytest /opt/mem20/mem20cliz -q
```

the suite asserts the property that matters most: the human path is unchanged,
and json mode never leaks human text to stdout.

subsystems.name: mem20controlz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20controlz

unified control plane for the mem20 fleet: per-subsystem panels (rest first,
standardised cli fallback), the websites manager for dns, site inventory, systemd
health, journals and cloudflare pages, and the **dreams manager** for reviewing
dreams and keeping the ones worth keeping.

one fastapi process serves both the api and the built frontend from a single
origin, so there is no second web server to operate.

## run it

the service is managed by systemd on this host:

```sh
systemctl status mem20controlz          # 127.0.0.1:8890
systemctl restart mem20controlz
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8890/api/health
```

to run it in the foreground instead:

```sh
python3 -m mem20controlz --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8890
```

`python -m mem20controlz --describe` prints the websites manager manifest.

## authentication

two independent layers, either of which admits a request:

1. **cloudflare access** — a verified identity header, trusted only when
   `control_trust_cf_access` is set. it is off by default, because a client can
   forge that header when the service is not actually behind access.
2. **admin password** — a constant-time check that mints an hmac-signed session
   cookie valid for 12 hours.

both read from `/opt/mem20/secrets/.env` (or the environment):

| key | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mem20_control_password` | admin password |
| `mem20_control_secret` | session signing secret |
| `control_trust_cf_access` | set to `1` only when behind cloudflare access |

**the secrets file wins; the environment is only a fallback.** that order is
load-bearing and was the other way round, which was a real defect. `llm.py` runs a
dotenv load at import time and copies *every* key it finds — not just api keys,
despite what its own docstring says — into `os.environ`. this service imports it
transitively through `mem20dreamz`, so the admin password and the signing secret
were snapshotted into the process environment at boot. rotating either one in the
file then appeared to do nothing until the unit was restarted, and a rotated
signing secret left already-issued cookies verifiable. now a rotation takes effect
on the next request, with no restart. an environment-only deployment still works,
because the environment is consulted when the file has no value for the key.

**failing closed is deliberate.** with no password configured nothing can log
in, and with no signing secret `post /api/auth/login` returns `503` rather than
handing out an unsigned session. `/api/health` and `/api/auth/status` stay open
so a load balancer can probe the service and the login screen can ask what the
auth setup is.

## status honesty

the registry never reports a panel as `ok` unless a verified surface answered.

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | rest or cli probe confirmed the surface |
| `degraded` | probe reached it and it failed the contract |
| `unreachable` | probe could not reach it at all |
| `no-health` | the cli runs but exposes no `health` verb — a probe gap, not a fault |
| `unknown` | nothing could be confirmed |

`no-health` exists so that a working cli without a health verb is not reported
as broken. a unit that does not exist is reported as `not-found`, not
`inactive`, because "inactive" would claim a service had started and failed.

every registry response carries `cached`, `age_s` and `stale`. a full sweep
spawns ~30 subprocesses and takes seconds, so it is cached and refreshed in the
background; the age is always reported so cached data is never mistaken for a
live reading. the cache key includes the probe timeouts, because evidence
gathered with a 15s budget is not the same evidence as a 2s budget.

## api

| method | path | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| get | `/api/health` | open |
| get | `/api/auth/status` | open; reports posture + whether this caller is admitted |
| post | `/api/auth/login` | `{"password": "..."}` |
| post | `/api/auth/logout` | |
| get | `/api/registry` | cached fleet panels |
| get | `/api/cli/coverage` | cli contract audit (slow: runs a full audit) |
| get | `/api/websites/manifest` | |
| get | `/api/websites/sites` | |
| get | `/api/websites/dns` | `?zone=&pattern=` |
| post | `/api/websites/dns` | `{"zone","type","name","content","proxied","ttl"}` |
| delete | `/api/websites/dns/{id}` | `?zone=` |
| get | `/api/websites/health` | systemd unit health |
| get | `/api/websites/logs` | `?unit=&lines=` (1–5000) |
| get | `/api/websites/pages` | cloudflare pages projects |
| get | `/api/dreams/manifest` | what the dreams manager can do |
| get | `/api/dreams` | `?kind=&include_hollow=&only_unpromoted=&limit=` |
| get | `/api/dreams/idle-stats` | idle inventory + who holds the run lock |
| get | `/api/dreams/hollow` | read-only census of failed-call lineages |
| get | `/api/dreams/runs` | background run jobs |
| get | `/api/dreams/runs/{job_id}` | one job, with a bounded log tail |
| post | `/api/dreams/runs` | `{"dream_id","iterations"}` → starts a job, returns at once |
| get | `/api/dreams/{dream_id}` | one lineage in full, artifact included |
| get | `/api/dreams/{dream_id}/chain` | ordered cids and any uncommitted iterations |
| post | `/api/dreams/{dream_id}/verify` | re-prove every node |
| post | `/api/dreams/{dream_id}/promote` | `{"force":bool}` → portable roadmap pack |
| post | `/api/dreams` | `{"seed","foundation","kind"}` → new lineage, free |

unmatched `/api/*` paths return `404`, never the spa shell — a mistyped api
route must not come back as a `200` with html.

## dreams

the review surface for `mem20dreamz`. it imports the engine as a library rather
than shelling out to `mem20-dream`, so there is one implementation of the rules
instead of two that can disagree. the exception is a run: that is spawned as the
engine's own cli, because the cli owns the lock discipline and the exit-code
contract, and reimplementing them here is how two runs end up dreaming at once.

four things it is careful about, each because the alternative is a quiet lie:

* **the list never carries an artifact.** a lineage's artifact reaches hundreds of
  kilobytes and the list is polled, so rows carry counts and flags only. the
  detail view fetches one dream, artifact included.
* **hollow lineages are flagged, not hidden.** thirty-nine on this host recorded a
  provider error where a panel result should be. a hollow filter exists, and when
  it hides rows the response says how many.
* **a refusal is never flattened.** the engine refuses promotion on a hollow
  lineage and on a damaged chain; those are different facts with different
  remedies, so both are passed through with the engine's own wording. a refusal
  is a `409` with the reason, or a `200` with `promoted: false` — never a generic
  error.
* **"kept" is labelled by how it is derived.** it is read from the promotions
  directory on disk, not from the ledger, so a pack written elsewhere would not
  show up. the response says which.

### runs are jobs, not requests

an iteration is a full panel of models; five iterations measure at six to seven
minutes, against a twenty-second browser timeout. so `post /api/dreams/runs`
spawns the engine cli and returns a job id at once, and the tab polls it.

the exit codes stay distinct, because they are different facts:

| exit | reported as | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `done` | every requested iteration ran |
| 2 | `paused` | a provider dropped; everything that landed was kept |
| 3 | `refused` | another run holds the lock |
| other | `failed` | see the log tail |

`paused` is deliberately not `failed`: telling an operator a partially-successful
run failed invites them to throw away work that is mostly intact.

run records are held **in memory only**, and `get /api/dreams/runs` says so. a
restart forgets them — deliberately, because a job record that outlived its
process would report a dead run as live.

a run is bounded at 20 iterations and at the ceiling the idle service itself uses.
past the ceiling the child is killed and the job is re

subsystems.description: Native mem20 CoreAI absorption — real model serving (tensor engine + ollama LLM), real batching, quantization, distillation, evaluation
subsystems.name: mem20corez
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20corez

native mem20 absorption of coreai: **real** model serving, inference
batching, quantization, distillation and evaluation.

everything here computes. there are no canned values, no print-fakes, no
`notimplementederror` stubs. every number a test or endpoint returns is the
result of actual arithmetic or actual measured inference.

## what is real

| capability | real implementation |
|---|---|
| **serving** | fastapi + uvicorn server (`serve`). two genuine inference paths: (1) a numpy character-mlp "tensor engine" loaded from a real `.npz` weight file — every completion/embedding is a real matrix multiply; (2) a local **ollama** llm backend (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`) that generates real text through the local openai-compatible endpoint. |
| **batching** | a real dynamic-batching scheduler: concurrent requests are grouped up to `max_batch_size` or `batch_timeout_ms`, and the tensor engine executes the whole batch as **one stacked matmul**. results preserve input order; latencies are measured. |
| **quantization** | real int8 / block-int4 / fp16 quantization of real weight tensors with min-max scales and zero-points; writes a real quantized `.npz`; reports real compression (from actual file bytes) and real error (mse / max-abs of dequantization). |
| **distillation** | real teacher→student training: a smaller network is trained with the exact gradient of kl-divergence (or mse) against the teacher's temperature-scaled soft outputs. accuracies and perplexities are measured on real evaluation text. |
| **evaluation** | real accuracy, per-class precision/recall/f1, perplexity, and measured latency percentiles from actually running the model. |

## served endpoints

- `get  /health` — real tensor-engine status + ollama reachability
- `get  /v1/models` — registered tensor models (`mem20corez://…`) + ollama models
- `post /v1/chat/completions` — real llm chat (ollama, e.g. `qwen2.5-coder:0.5b`)
- `post /v1/completions` — real completion (tensor engine or ollama)
- `post /v1/embeddings` — real vector embeddings from the tensor engine
- `get  /v1/stats` — real measured server/batcher statistics

## quick start

```bash
pip install -e .            # into .venv or your venv (numpy-only, no torch)

mem20corez serve --port 8006

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8006/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8006/v1/completions \
     -d '{"model":"mem20corez://demo-char","prompt":"the quick brown fox","max_tokens":16}'
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8006/v1/chat/completions \
     -d '{"model":"qwen2.5-coder:0.5b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in one short sentence."}]}'
```

the `serve` command trains and registers the built-in `demo-char` tensor model
on first run (a few seconds, real training, real weights written to
`/opt/mem20/corez/models/demo-char.npz`).

cli: `mem20corez test` runs a real self-test (`infer`, `quantize`, `distill`,
`evaluate`, `benchmark` subcommands all do real work).

## tests

```bash
pytest            # real assertions on real computed values, no mocking
```

## honesty notes

- llm text generation requires a reachable ollama endpoint (`localhost:11434`
  by default, see `ollama_url` in `coreaiconfig`). without ollama the tensor
  engine still serves real embeddings and completions.
- the tensor engine is intentionally tiny (a character mlp) so the whole
  pipeline — train, quantize, distill, evaluate, serve — is cpu-fast and fully
  deterministic. it is a real model, not a placeholder.
- no gpu acceleration is claimed; latency numbers are real cpu measurements.

subsystems.description: cleanroom mem20 crews on mem20
subsystems.name: mem20crewz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20crewz

**roadmap-backed multi-agent crews on the mem20 substrate.**

mem20crewz is a cleanroom implementation of agent / task / crew / flow primitives. every crew run is a first-class roadmap: phases move planned → in_progress → completed/blocked and are persisted. reasoning goes through a pluggable brain (real cogbrain or deterministic fakebrain for tests). delegation fans out over a2a peers. guardrails (epistemic veto, quarantine, plan-execution) are enforced on every step.

zero dependency on any legacy "mem20 crews" package — this surface imports only mem20 natives.

## quick start

```bash
# from a clean environment
pip install -e "./mem20crewz[dev]"
python -m pytest mem20crewz/tests -q          # 52 tests

# offline deterministic demo (no api keys)
python -m mem20crewz.demo.demo_crew --fake
```

## repository layout

```
mem20crewz/
  __init__.py      public exports
  neural.py        brain (abc), cogbrain, fakebrain
  agents.py        agent
  tasks.py         task, taskoutcome
  crew.py          crew, crewresult
  flow.py          flow
  guardrails.py    guards (epistemic veto, quarantine, plan-execution)
  roadmap.py       roadmap persistence
  a2a.py           peer delegation
  ecosystem.py     4.0 cross-subsystem governor
  cli.py           operator cli
  tests/
```

## cross-subsystem wiring (mem20 4.0 criterion 6)

a crew is a set of agents doing work in sequence, so every crew run is also a
memory, verification and budget question. `ecosystem.py` is that seam — the
crew's own pre-flight/post-flight path.

| subsystem | function called | what it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_engine` | `memory.recall` / `memory.remember` | what is grounded before the crew starts |
| `mem20verify` | `linters.all_checks` (each invoked) | is the code the crew produced structurally sound |
| `mem20dreamz` | `verdicts.fidelity_verdict` / `divergence` | does the output still serve the brief |
| `mem20kilnz` | `budgets.check_triangles` | is the claimed asset within its authored budget |
| `mem20corez` | `mlp.charmlp.perplexity` | how unlike the corpus is the output |
| `mem20cliz` | `build_envelope` / `split_json_flag` | the fleet's shared `--json` envelope |

the epistemic veto (`guardrails.guards`) is the crew's *own* mechanism and is
not counted as external wiring.

`crewgovernor.prepare()` runs before the crew; `judge()` runs after it. a
subsystem that is missing or raises is recorded as `{"ok": false, "error": ...}`
and never aborts the crew — but `report.clear` is then `false`, so a caller can
refuse to ship an unverified run instead of guessing.

## runnable example

```bash
cd mem20crewz
mem20_store_path=/tmp/cz-demo python3 - <<'py'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "."); sys.path.insert(0, "..")
import ecosystem

out = ecosystem.run_governor(
    "what is the prop triangle budget?",
    "the prop budget is 4000 triangles.\n"
    "```python\ndef within(n):\n    return n <= 6000\n```",
    topic="crew.readme",
)
print("clear:", out["clear"])
print("subsystems:", out["subsystems"])
print("lint clean:", out["lint"]["clean"],
      "| budget ok:", out["budget"]["within_budget"],
      "| fidelity:", out["fidelity"]["fidelity"],
      "| perplexity:", round(out["surprise"]["perplexity"], 2))
py
```

real output of the block above, run on this branch:

```
clear: true
subsystems: ['memory_engine', 'mem20verify', 'mem20dreamz', 'mem20kilnz', 'mem20corez']
lint clean: true | budget ok: true | fidelity: 50 | perplexity: 59.17
```

## mcp surface (criterion 7)

registered in `mcp/tools/crewz_tools.py` and mixed into `mcp/server.py`:

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `crewz_status` | is the runtime importable, and what does it wire to |
| `crewz_ground` | grounded context before a crew starts |
| `crewz_govern` | judge a crew output before it ships (all five subsystems) |
| `crewz_guard` | the crew's own epistemic veto over a set of fact ids |

## tests

```bash
cd mem20crewz
python3 -m pytest tests/test_ecosystem.py -q
```

`tests/test_ecosystem.py` asserts on the values the *other* subsystems compute —
a crew outcome recorded through the governor is read back by the engine's own
`recall` and labelled `agent_generated`, a known-bad snippet is caught by
`mem20verify`, an over-budget triangle count is rejected by `mem20kilnz` — so
the wiring is exercised, not merely declared.

## verification

```bash
cd /opt/mem20
python3 scripts/renovation/conformance.py mem20crewz
```

# rm-005 — cross-runtime event lattice

**outcome:** connect independent runtimes through typed events, durable streams, and reactive subscriptions
**breakthrough:** the ecosystem behaves like one nervous system without becoming monolithic
**version:** 4.0.0 · **subsystem:** `mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez`

the lattice is the causality layer of the mem20 estate. it emits typed events,
orders them, links them into a vector-clock dag, and merges independent
lattices into one. since 4.0 it is wired into the substrate rather than
standing alone: every lattice event can be persisted to durable memory,
searched multi-hop, announced to the fleet gateway, verified for ledger
integrity, and compacted for the wire.

## install

mem20 is **not on pypi**. install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bythewayz66-glitch/mem20.git
cd mem20
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## quick start — runnable example

this is the whole seam in one script: emit an event, link a child to it
causally, persist both, announce them to the fleet, read them back, and report
on the merged lattice. run it from the repo root.

```bash
cd mem20
mem20_store_path=/tmp/mem20-lattice-demo python3 - <<'py'
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez")

from mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez import domain, integration

parent = domain.emit("session.start", {"user": "u-1"}, source="local")
out = integration.emit_and_record(
    "session.view", {"page": "/pricing"}, lattice="web", source="edge", parent=parent
)
print("event id       :", out["event"]["id"])
print("parent         :", out["event"]["parent"])
print("vector clock   :", out["event"]["vector"])
print("memory topic   :", out["memory_topic"])
print("announced by   :", out["announced"]["agent_name"])

rows = integration.recall_events("web", "session.view")
print("recalled rows  :", len(rows))
print("recalled body  :", json.loads(rows[0]["content"])["payload"])

report = integration.lattice_report(
    [{"events": [parent]}, {"events": [out["event"]]}], name="web"
)
print("lattice count  :", report["count"])
print("by type        :", report["by_type"])
print("sources        :", report["sources"])
print("causal links   :", report["causal_links"])
print("inventory total:", report["inventory"]["total"])
py
```

```
causal links   : 1
inventory total: 312
```

## cli

```bash
# emit + link + persist + announce
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez emit \
    --type click --payload '{"x": 1}' --lattice web --source edge

# operational report for a merged lattice
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez report --lattice web --lattices 2 --events 2

# round-trip the memory engine and exit non-zero if the ledger is unfaithful
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez verify

# measured estate inventory counts
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez inventory

# multi-hop search over lattice history
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez search \
    "which runtime emitted the first failure and what did it cause"

# quantize a numeric payload for the wire
python3 -m mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez compact 1.0 2.0 3.0 4.0 --bits 8
```

## mcp tools

registered on the mem20 mcp server (`mcp/server.py` → `latticetoolsmixin`):

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `lattice_emit` | emit, causally link, persist and announce one event |
| `lattice_report` | merged-lattice health + substrate health in one call |
| `lattice_recall` | read back persisted events for a lattice/type |
| `lattice_verify` | round-trip the memory engine, report ledger fidelity |
| `lattice_search` | decompose a compound causality question into sub-retrievals |

## estate wiring (criterion 6)

every one of these is a real call on a tested path — see
`mem20crossruntimeeventlatticez/tests/test_integration.py`.

| mem20 project | api used | where |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_engine` | `memory.remember` / `memory.recall` / `memory.status` | `integration.remember_event`, `recall_events`, `memory_status` |
| `memory_engine` | `retrieval_v2.decompose_query` | `integration.search_history` |
| `toolchest` | `catalog.load_inventory` | `integration.capability_inventory` |
| `gateway` | `hermes_gateway.broadcast` / `register_agent` / `load_names` | `integration.announce` |
| `mem20verify` | `dataintegrity.check` | `integration.verify_memory_integrity` |
| `mem20ops` | `memchecks.identity_check` | `integration.identity_report` |
| `mem20corez` | `quantizer.quantize_tensor` | `integration.compact_payload` |

### two estate traps this subsystem has to handle

both are real and both are documented in `_bootstrap.py` rather than papered
over:

1. **shim shadowing.** `mem20corez/__init__.py` is a version-only shim sitting
   next to the real package at `mem20corez/mem20corez/`. with the repo root on
   `sys.path`, `import mem20corez` resolves to the shim and `quantizer` is
   unreachable. `_bootstrap.ensure_estate_path()` puts the inner package parent
   ahead of the repo root and evicts an already-imported shim.
2. **`memory` shim vs engine.** the repo root ships a `memory.py` that
   re-exports `memory_engine.memory`. `mem20verify.dataintegrity.check()`
   rebinds `entries`/`ledger` on whatever `import memory` returns, so if the
   shim wins, the rebinding lands on the shim and the check reports 0
   round-trips while looking like a data-integrity failure.
   `verify_memory_integrity()` binds the real engine module first.

# mem20cviz — computer-vision-inference subsystem

imagined by mem20 (imagination_dream, 3 iterations, 2026-09-20) as the
`cv.infer` capability-plane subsystem, then **built real** here as a locally
executable package. designed to fit the mem20 pattern: a versioned capability
descriptor registered in the ucg, typed i/o, signed braid journal per inference,
honest boundaries — no fabricated cv.

## what it does

| mode   | engine                              | real? | meaning                                     |
|--------|-------------------------------------|-------|---------------------------------------------|
| `real` | `mem20cviz.classical` (numpy/pil)   | yes   | actual pixel math: edges, colors, stats, fixed-dim embedding |
| `sim`  | `mem20cviz.simulator`               | no    | deterministic contract proof, `simulated:true`, hash-derived |

the subsystem **never pretends to see**. `sim` explicitly marks itself
simulated. `real` computes actual statistics of the actual image. a heavy nn
provider is an optional future hook — it is reported unavailable unless
actually configured, never faked.

## install

```bash
pip install -e /opt/mem20/mem20cviz
```

## usage

```bash
# real inference on a real image
fs-cv infer --image photo.png

# real inference from a base64 raw frame
fs-cv infer --frame-blob "$(base64 -w0 frame.rgb)"

# contract simulator
fs-cv sim --payload '{"mode":"sim"}'

# ucg descriptor
fs-cv descriptor

# http server (get /health, /.well-known/card, post /infer)
fs-cv serve --port 8783
```

## capability descriptor

- id: `cap.cv-inference.v1`
- version: `0.1.0`
- provider: `mem30.cv.inference`
- inputs: `image_path`, `frame_blob_b64`, `mode`, `options`
- outputs: `cv/features`, `cv/objects`, `cv/classifications`, `cv/embedding`

subsystems.description: Dream engine for mem20: iteration that improves rather than condenses, judged by a panel where every member is a different model.
subsystems.name: mem20dreamz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20dreamz — 4.0 promotion gate

the dream engine. iteration must **improve**, never **condense**.

## the defect this replaces

`cog/braid_dream_section.py:115` did `st["seed"] = out[:300]`. every iteration
read a 300-character tail of the previous output, so early structure could not
survive and each pass was a resample rather than a revision. measured on a real
run before the fix, the artifact oscillated `273 -> 993 -> 246 -> 11625` —
regeneration with a lottery. a lineage now keeps the artifact in full, every
intermediate version, an invention register, and its own evolving config.

## panel: one model per member

the owner's rule. a single-model panel makes its blind spot *systematic*: every
member can be confidently wrong the same way, and agreement is laundered into
consensus. eight distinct models, every one verified to answer on this host by a
real call. `assert_roster_valid()` **raises** on a duplicate model — it used to
deduplicate silently, which quietly deleted the `systems_inventor` role and left
the panel with a hole nobody could see.

## cross-subsystem wiring (mem20 4.0 criterion 6)

a dream is only worth keeping if it is *new* and *true*. the engine already
measures novelty against its own lineage; `mem20dreamz/ecosystem.py` adds the
estate's other half, so a candidate that invents a fact, ships broken code or
blows a triangle budget is caught before promotion.

| subsystem | function called | what it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_engine` | `memory.recall` / `memory.remember` | what the estate already knows about the seed |
| `mem20crewz` | `guardrails.guards.check_clearance` | may this dream rest on these facts |
| `mem20verify` | `linters.all_checks` (each invoked) | is the dream's code structurally sound |
| `mem20kilnz` | `budgets.check_triangles` | is the proposed asset within its authored budget |
| `mem20corez` | `mlp.charmlp.perplexity` | how unlike the corpus is the candidate |
| `mem20cliz` | `build_envelope` / `split_json_flag` | the fleet's shared `--json` envelope |

`dreamgate.ground()` runs before the dream; `judge()` runs after it. a subsystem
that is missing or raises is recorded as `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` and never
aborts the dream — but `report.promotable` is then `false`, so a caller can
refuse to promote an unverified candidate instead of guessing.

## runnable example

```bash
cd mem20dreamz
mem20_store_path=/tmp/dz-demo python3 - <<'py'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "."); sys.path.insert(0, "..")
from mem20dreamz import ecosystem

out = ecosystem.run_gate(
    "dream.mesh",
    "a lighter prop mesh at 4000 triangles.\n"
    "```python\ndef within(n):\n    return n <= 6000\n```",
)
print("promotable:", out["promotable"])
print("subsystems:", out["subsystems"])
print("lint clean:", out["lint"]["clean"],
      "| budget ok:", out["budget"]["within_budget"],
      "| perplexity:", round(out["distance"]["perplexity"], 2))
py
```

real output of the block above, run on this branch:

```
promotable: true
subsystems: ['memory_engine', 'mem20crewz', 'mem20verify', 'mem20kilnz', 'mem20corez']
lint clean: true | budget ok: true | perplexity: 58.84
```

## mcp surface (criterion 7)

registered in `mcp/tools/dreamz_tools.py` and mixed into `mcp/server.py`:

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `dreamz_status` | is the engine importable, and what does it wire to |
| `dreamz_ground` | what the estate already knows about a seed |
| `dreamz_gate` | judge a candidate before promotion (all five subsystems) |
| `dreamz_estate` | installed vs claimed vs phantom subsystems |

## tests

```bash
cd mem20dreamz
python3 -m pytest tests/test_ecosystem.py -q
```

`tests/test_ecosystem.py` asserts on the values the *other* subsystems compute —
a dream recorded through the gate is read back by the engine's own `recall` and
labelled `agent_generated`, a known-bad snippet is caught by `mem20verify`, an
over-budget triangle count is rejected by `mem20kilnz` — so the wiring is
exercised, not merely declared.

## verification

```bash
cd /opt/mem20
python3 scripts/renovation/conformance.py mem20dreamz
```

# mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz — edge-to-cloud intelligence continuum (rm-214)

**outcome:** run one workload fluidly across local devices, private servers, peers, and paid clouds.  
**breakthrough:** compute placement becomes invisible, resilient, and cost-aware.

this subsystem is a real, first-class continuum control plane: typed domain logic, a durable sqlite wal state plane, a service that owns placement/dispatch/failover, cross-subsystem judgements from six **unique** peers (a different set from `mem20causalroutingbrainz`), a cli, a json http api, a served operator cockpit, and a `docs/app` monitor.

## what it does

- **invisible placement:** callers declare constraints (`required_capabilities`, latency/cost ceilings, privacy zone, resilience, preferred tiers, priority, size) — not machine names. the scheduler scores feasible targets across `local`, `edge`, `private`, `peer`, and `cloud`.
- **resilient execution:** failed/degraded/draining sources produce explicit migration/failover plans. migration semantics are verified through the zero-downtime migration brain (unverified cutover is refused/rolled back in the semantic check).
- **cost-aware:** execution cost, egress/transport cost, pipeline economics, and market signals influence placement and are returned in decisions.
- **honest decisions:** every placement returns the chosen target, score, confidence, components/weights, alternatives, and bottlenecks. peer signals are reported (fail-open) — never hidden.

## architecture

| layer | file | responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| domain | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/domain.py` | tiers/status/state enums, `target`/`workload` validation and capacity accounting, latency/cost/privacy/capability checks, weighted scoring, `place_workload`, `failover_plan`, `migration_plan`, `continuum_health`. pure (no i/o). |
| state plane | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/store.py` | sqlite wal: versioned targets/workloads, append-only placements, migrations, ordered events, snapshots/restore, idempotency keys, conflict detection. |
| ecosystem | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/ecosystem.py` | six unique peer adapters with real calls and fail-open reporting. |
| service | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/service.py` | target registry, submit/place/dispatch/complete, failover, migration planning, status/events/metrics/snapshot/restore, `doctor`/`simulate`/`benchmark`. |
| runtime | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/runtime.py` | cli + `threadinghttpserver` json api + static cockpit (`web/`), cors, error mapping (`validationerror`→400, `notfounderror`→404, `conflicterror`→409). |
| web | `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz/web/` | operator cockpit: targets, workloads, dispatch/failover, events, doctor/simulate. |

## unique cross-subsystem wiring (criterion 6)

**rule:** the ≥5 cross-module peers must be a **different set on each subsystem** (no reused template). this subsystem uses a continuum-specific set, different from `mem20causalroutingbrainz`:

| peer | real calls used | what it contributes |
|---|---|---|
| `mem20federatedresearchgridz` | `register_node`, `distribute_task`, `federated_round`, `grid_health` | federated task distribution/health across continuum tiers |
| `mem20pipez` | `stage_cost`, `pipeline_cost`, `bottleneck`, `optimize_throughput`, `cost_breakdown` | cost-aware pipeline/placement economics |
| `mem20edgetransportfabricz` | `route_path`, `qos_class`, `allocate_bandwidth`, `transport_health` | transport path, qos class, bandwidth allocation/health |
| `mem20causalroutingbrainz` | `zerodowntimemigrationbrain.begin`, `write/read`, `verify_and_cutover`/rollback semantics | verified zero-downtime migration semantics (refuse unverified cutover) |
| `mem20globalcapabilitymarketplacez` | `list_capability`, `search_marketplace`, `match`, `transaction`, `marketplace_health` | capability discovery/matching across tiers/providers |
| `mem20resourceexchangemarketz` | `list_resource`, `buy`, `price_history`, `market_health` | resource pricing/market signals |

all are invoked on normal service paths (register/submit/place/dispatch/status/doctor) and exercised by the subsystem’s tests.

## cli

```bash
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db status
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db doctor
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db simulate
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db benchmark --iterations 20
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db target add --id local-lab --tier local --cpu 8 --memory 16 --latency 2 --cost 0 --bandwidth 10000 --capabilities compute,render
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db target add --id cloud-gpu --tier cloud --cpu 32 --memory 64 --latency 90 --cost 0.4 --bandwidth 10000 --capabilities compute,gpu,render
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db target list
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db workload submit --id render-1 --cpu 2 --memory 4 --size 0.5 --capabilities render --max-latency 200 --resilience high
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db dispatch --id render-1
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db workload complete render-1 --reason done
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db failover render-1 --reason outage
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db events --limit 20
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db snapshot --label before-change
python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store /tmp/ctm.db serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8791
```

## runnable example (verified)

```bash
cd /opt/mem20
s=/tmp/ctm-demo.db
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store "$s" \
  target add --id local-lab --tier local --cpu 8 --memory 16 --latency 2 --cost 0 --bandwidth 10000 --capabilities compute,render
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store "$s" \
  target add --id cloud-gpu --tier cloud --cpu 32 --memory 64 --latency 90 --cost 0.4 --bandwidth 10000 --capabilities compute,gpu,render
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store "$s" \
  workload submit --id render-1 --cpu 2 --memory 4 --size 0.5 --capabilities render --max-latency 200 --resilience high
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz --store "$s" \
  dispatch --id render-1
```

observed (real run, key fields):

```text
submit: ok=true chosen_preview=local-lab score=0.992454
signals: federated/cost/resource_market all ok
dispatch: 1 chosen=local-lab state=running
peer_signals: federated/cost/capability_market/resource_market/transport all ok
migration_semantics: phase=cutover verified=true
```

`submit` returns a full `placement_preview` (chosen, score, confidence, feasible alternatives, components, bottlenecks) plus federated/cost/resource market signals. `dispatch` reserves capacity, runs the workload, records the placement, and returns transport/capability/resource/federated/cost signals and migration semantics. the cloud target remains a feasible alternative (visible in the decision) but local wins on latency/cost for this constraint set.

## http api

the server (`serve`) hosts the same json api and the static cockpit at `/`.

| method | path | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| get | `/api/status` | continuum health, tiers, metrics, transport signal |
| get | `/api/targets`, `/api/targets/{id}` | targets |
| post | `/api/targets` | register target |
| post | `/api/targets/{id}/status` | set target status |
| delete | `/api/targets/{id}` | delete target |
| get/post | `/api/workloads`, `/api/workloads/{id}` | list/get/submit workloads |
| post | `/api/dispatch

subsystems.name: mem20edgetransportfabricz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20edgetransportfabricz — edge transport fabric (rm-077)

**outcome:** move bounded data and commands across intermittently connected nodes.  
**breakthrough:** devices and remote sites remain integrated even with poor connectivity.

this subsystem is a real, first-class transport control plane: typed domain logic (legacy-compatible primitives + advanced fabric model), a durable sqlite wal state plane, a service that owns topology/admission/routing/reservations/reroute, cross-subsystem judgements from six **unique** peers (a different set from `mem20causalroutingbrainz` #300 and `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz` #301), a cli, a json http api, a served operator cockpit, and a `docs/app` monitor.

## what it does

- **legacy-compatible transport primitives:** `route_path(src,dst,nodes)` (neighbor map), `qos_class(latency_ms,priority)`, `allocate_bandwidth(total,demands)`, `transport_health(links)` — preserved for existing callers (including `mem20edgetocloudintelligencecontinuumz`).
- **fabric routing:** bandwidth-aware shortest path over node/link topology with link status (up/degraded/intermittent/down), latency/jitter/loss/cost/reservation weights, qos/sla checks, and alternative paths.
- **intermittent connectivity:** when strict constraints cannot be met but intermittent delivery is acceptable, the fabric returns an explicit degraded/bounded plan instead of hiding failure.
- **admission & capacity:** token-bucket/traffic admission signals, bandwidth reservation/release, congestion/utilization/health.
- **resilience:** fault containment/circuit-breaker signals, self-healing retry semantics, causal route influence, recovery planning, and explicit reroute plans.
- **observability:** append-only events, placement journal, telemetry stream publication, snapshots/restore, status/doctor/simulate/benchmark.

## architecture

| layer | file | responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| domain | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/domain.py` | legacy-compatible functions + `fabricnode`/`fabriclink`/`flowdemand`/`pathdecision`, bandwidth-aware routing, qos/sla, admission, reservation, reroute, fabric/transport health. pure (no i/o). |
| state plane | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/store.py` | sqlite wal: versioned nodes/links/flows, events, placements, idempotency, snapshots/restore. |
| ecosystem | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/ecosystem.py` | six unique peer adapters with real calls and fail-open reporting. |
| service | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/service.py` | topology crud, admit/route/reserve/release/reroute, status/doctor/events/placements/snapshots, simulate/benchmark; peer signals on real operations. |
| runtime | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/runtime.py` | cli + `threadinghttpserver` json api + static cockpit (`web/`), cors, error mapping (400/404/409). |
| web | `mem20edgetransportfabricz/web/` | operator cockpit. |

## unique cross-subsystem wiring (criterion 6)

**rule:** the ≥5 cross-module peers must be a **different set on each subsystem**. this fabric uses a transport-specific set, different from #300 and #301:

| peer | real calls used | what it contributes |
|---|---|---|
| `mem20meshz.mem20meshz.meshes.selfhealing.domain` | `selfhealingconnectormesh.call/delay_for` | resilient transient delivery/retry with backoff/jitter |
| `mem20autonomoustrafficcontrollerz.domain` | `tokenbucket.allow/retry_after`, `leakybucket` | admission control/backpressure for link/flow demand |
| `mem20faultcontainmentcellsz.domain` | `faultcontainmentcells.call/state` | circuit breaking/fail-fast containment |
| `mem20causalroutingbrainz.domain` | `route_by_cause`, `causal_effect`, `confounder_adjust`, `intervention_value` | causal/weighted route influence |
| `mem20autonomousrecoverydirectorz.domain` | `triage`, `rollback_plan`, `remediate`, `recovery_time`, `health_after` | incident recovery/remediation planning |
| `mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz.domain` | `create_stream/publish/subscribe/consume/throughput/lag` | fabric telemetry/flow event stream |

all are invoked on normal paths (node/link upsert, admit/route/reserve/reroute/status/doctor/simulate) and exercised by the subsystem’s tests.

## cli

```bash
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 status
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 doctor
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 simulate
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 benchmark --iterations 20
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 node add --id edge-a --capacity 1000
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 node add --id edge-b --capacity 1000
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 link add --src edge-a --dst edge-b --bandwidth 100 --latency 10 --status up
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 flow admit --id flow-1 --src edge-a --dst edge-b --demand 5 --priority 2 --max-latency 100
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 flow route --src edge-a --dst edge-b --demand 5
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 flow reroute flow-1 --avoid edge-a->edge-b --reason failure
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 events --limit 20
python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db state/transport.sqlite3 serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8782
```

## runnable example (verified)

```bash
cd /opt/mem20
db=/tmp/etf-demo.sqlite3
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db "$db" node add --id edge-a --capacity 1000 >/dev/null
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db "$db" node add --id edge-b --capacity 1000 >/dev/null
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db "$db" link add --src edge-a --dst edge-b --bandwidth 100 --latency 10 --status up >/dev/null
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20edgetransportfabricz --db "$db" flow admit --id flow-1 --src edge-a --dst edge-b --demand 5 --priority 2 --max-latency 100
```

observed (real run, key fields):

```text
ok=true
decision: admitted=true path=['edge-a','edge-b'] latency_ms=10.0 bottleneck_mbps=100.0 qos=premium
signals: causal/traffic/containment/mesh/telemetry all ok
sla: ok=true (bandwidth, path_exists)
```

`admit` computes a bandwidth-aware path, checks qos/sla, records the durable flow/placement, and returns peer signals (causal route, traffic admission, fault containment, mesh resilience, telemetry). poor/intermittent links return explicit degraded plans/reasons rather than hidden failure.

| get | `/api/events?since=&limit=`, `/api/placements?flow_id=` | event/placement journals |
| get | `/api/doctor`, `/api/metrics` | peer probe and store metrics |
| post | `/api/snapshot`, `/api/restore`, `/api/simulate`, `/api/benchmark` | state/scenarios |
| get | `/`, `/app.js`, `/style.css` | operator cockpit |

errors are json with real status codes (400 validation, 404 missing, 409 conflict).

## web surfaces

- **docs/app integration:** `docs/app/transport/index.html` — static estate monitor connecting to the fabric api (`?api=`/stored base url). linked from `docs/app/readme.md`. (compiled vite assets are not modified.)

subsystems.description: mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz first-class module
subsystems.name: mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz
subsystems.readme_text:
# rm-074 — event stream superhighway

**outcome:** route high-volume typed events across local, edge, and cloud runtimes
**breakthrough:** every product can react to live data without custom plumbing
**version:** 4.0.0 · **subsystem:** `mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz`

the superhighway is the transport layer of the mem20 estate. it routes typed
events, tracks per-subscriber offsets and lag, and — since 4.0 — it is wired
into the substrate rather than standing alone: every routed event can be
persisted to durable memory, searched multi-hop, announced to the fleet
gateway, verified for ledger integrity, screened for leaked credentials, and
compacted for the wire.

## install

mem20 is **not on pypi**. install from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bythewayz66-glitch/mem20.git
cd mem20
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## quick start — runnable example

this is the whole seam in one script: publish an event, persist it, announce it
to the fleet, read it back, and report on the stream. run it from the repo root.

```bash
cd mem20
mem20_store_path=/tmp/mem20-demo-store python3 - <<'py'
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz")

from mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz import domain, integration

stream = domain.create_stream("orders")
domain.subscribe(stream, "billing")

out = integration.publish_and_persist(
    stream, "order.created", {"id": 7, "total": 42.5}, key="o-7"
)
print("event seq      :", out["event"]["seq"])
print("memory topic   :", out["memory_topic"])
print("announced by   :", out["announced"]["agent_name"])
print("screening clean:", out["screening"]["clean"])

rows = integration.recall_events("orders", "order.created")
print("recalled rows  :", len(rows))
print("recalled body  :", json.loads(rows[0]["content"])["payload"])

report = integration.stream_report(stream)
print("throughput/min :", report["throughput_per_min"])
print("lag            :", report["lag"])
print("inventory total:", report["inventory"]["total"])
py
```

real output from a run of the block above:

```
event seq      : 1
memory topic   : eventstream.orders.order.created
announced by   : eventstream-orders
screening clean: true
recalled rows  : 1
recalled body  : {'id': 7, 'total': 42.5}
throughput/min : 1.0
lag            : {'billing': 1}
inventory total: 312
```

## cli

```bash
# publish + persist + announce
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz publish \
    --stream orders --type order.created --payload '{"id": 7}' --key o-7

# operational report (stream + substrate in one object)
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz report --stream orders --subscriber billing

# round-trip the memory engine and exit non-zero if the ledger is unfaithful
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz verify

# measured estate inventory counts
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz inventory

# multi-hop search over the event log
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz search \
    "what is the p95 latency and which partition is hot"

# quantize a numeric payload for the wire
python3 -m mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz compact 1.0 2.0 3.0 4.0 --bits 8
```

## mcp tools

registered on the mem20 mcp server (`mcp/server.py` → `eventstreamtoolsmixin`):

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `stream_publish` | publish, persist and announce one event; returns the memory id |
| `stream_report` | stream health + substrate health in one call |
| `stream_recall` | read back persisted events for a stream/type |
| `stream_verify` | round-trip the memory engine, report ledger fidelity |
| `stream_search` | decompose a compound telemetry question into sub-retrievals |

## estate wiring (criterion 6)

every one of these is a real call on a tested path — see
`mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz/tests/test_integration.py`.

| mem20 project | api used | where |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_engine` | `memory.remember` / `memory.recall` / `memory.status` | `integration.remember_event`, `recall_events`, `memory_status` |
| `memory_engine` | `retrieval_v2.decompose_query` | `integration.search_events` |
| `toolchest` | `catalog.load_inventory` | `integration.capability_inventory` |
| `gateway` | `hermes_gateway.broadcast` / `register_agent` / `load_names` | `integration.announce` |
| `mem20verify` | `dataintegrity.check` | `integration.verify_memory_integrity` |
| `mem20ops` | `memchecks.identity_check` | `integration.identity_report` |
| `mem20corez` | `quantizer.quantize_tensor` | `integration.compact_payload` |
| `mem20secretz` | `sweep.classify` | `integration.screen_payload` |

### three estate traps this subsystem has to handle

all three are real and all three are documented in `_bootstrap.py` rather than
papered over:

1. **shim shadowing.** `mem20corez/__init__.py` is a version-only shim sitting
   next to the real package at `mem20corez/mem20corez/`. with the repo root on
   `sys.path`, `import mem20corez` resolves to the shim and `quantizer` is
   unreachable. `_bootstrap.ensure_estate_path()` puts the inner package parent
   ahead of the repo root and evicts an already-imported shim.
2. **`memory` shim vs engine.** the repo root ships a `memory.py` that
   re-exports `memory_engine.memory`. `mem20verify.dataintegrity.check()`
   rebinds `entries`/`ledger` on whatever `import memory` returns, so if the
   shim wins, the rebinding lands on the shim and the check reports 0
   round-trips while looking like a data-integrity failure.
   `verify_memory_integrity()` binds the real engine module first.
3. **`sweep` name collision.** `mem20secretz/__init__.py` re-exports the
   *function* `sweep`, which shadows the submodule of the same name on the
   package object — so `from mem20secretz import sweep` hands back a function
   with no `.classify`. the seam imports `from mem20secretz.sweep import
   classify` instead.

## tests

```bash
python3 -m pytest mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz -q
```

## conformance

```bash
python3 scripts/renovation/conformance.py mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz
```

## public api

```python
from mem20eventstreamsuperhighwayz import domain, integration

# domain — the stream itself
domain.create_stream(name) -> dict
domain.publish(stream, event_type, payload, key=none) -> dict
domain.subscribe(stream, subscriber_id, filter_type=none) -> dict
domain.consume(stream, subscriber_id, batch=10) -> list[dict]
domain.throughput(stream, window_s=60) -> float
domain.lag(stream, subscriber_id) -> int

# integration — the seam onto the estate
integration.publish_and_persist(stream, event_type, payload, key=none, announce_to_fleet=true) -> dict
integration.remember_event(stream, event, actor="eventstream") -> dict
integration.recall_events(stream_name, event_type=none) -> list[dict]
integration.stream_report(stream, window_s=60) -> dict
integration.search_events(query, k=5) -> dict
integration.capability_inventory() -> dict
integration.announce(stream, event, agent_name=none) -> dict
integration.verify_memory_integrity() -> dict
integration.identity_report() -> dict
integration.compact_payload(values, bits=8) -> dict
integration.screen_payload(payload) -> dict
```

subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20factoryz

procedural content generation for the mem20 estate: deterministic terrain, bsp dungeons, loot, assets, levels, narrative beats, and lightweight playtesting.

- **package**: `mem20factoryz`
- **python**: >= 3.11 (see `pyproject.toml`)
- **core property**: generation is seed-driven and deterministic for a given config

## install

from a mem20 checkout:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e mem20factoryz
```

## cli

```bash
# generate a level summary
mem20factoryz generate --seed 7 --width 32 --height 32

# preview terrain tiles
mem20factoryz terrain --seed 7 --width 16 --height 12

# write a deterministic texture (ppm) and sfx (wav)
mem20factoryz texture --seed 7 --resolution 16 --out /tmp/factoryz_texture.ppm
mem20factoryz audio --seed 7 --out /tmp/factoryz_sfx.wav

# narrative beats
mem20factoryz story --seed 7 --segments 5

# playtest a generated level
mem20factoryz playtest --seed 7 --runs 2

# built-in self-test
mem20factoryz test --seed 7
```

## python api

```python
from mem20factoryz.config import factoryconfig
from mem20factoryz.generator import terraingenerator, bspdungeongenerator, lootgenerator
from mem20factoryz.level import levelbuilder
from mem20factoryz.narrative import narrativeengine
from mem20factoryz.assets import assetsynthesizer, palette
from mem20factoryz.playtest import playtester

cfg = factoryconfig(seed=7, width=32, height=32)

# heightmap (list[list[float]]) and tile quantization
hmap = terraingenerator().generate(cfg)
tiles = terraingenerator().to_tiles(hmap, levels=4)

# bsp dungeon: walls/floors, rooms, spawn
dungeon = bspdungeongenerator().generate(cfg)
print(len(dungeon["rooms"]), dungeon["spawn"])

# deterministic loot
loot = lootgenerator().generate(factoryconfig(items_per_level=5))

# full level assembly
level = levelbuilder(cfg).build()
print(level.width, level.height, len(level.objectives))

# narrative and assets
beats = narrativeengine(seed=7).generate(segments=4)
synth = assetsynthesizer(factoryconfig(seed=7, asset_resolution=8))
pixels = synth.synthesise_texture(palette=palette.from_seed(7))
sfx = synth.synthesise_sfx()

# playtest
results = playtester(cfg).run(level, runs=2)
print(results[0].summary())
```

## development

```bash
python3 -m pytest mem20factoryz/mem20factoryz/tests -q
python3 scripts/renovation/conformance.py mem20factoryz
```

## notes

- outputs are procedural; keep `seed`/config stable for reproducible results.
- use the cli/api for real generation. do not treat placeholder values as generated assets.

subsystems.description: Family registry for the mem20*z packages: which family each package belongs to, what that family is for, and what would prove it.
subsystems.name: mem20famz
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20famz

the family registry for the `mem20*z` packages.

## why this exists

a clone audit hashed all 293 `mem20*z` packages with each package's own name
normalised out. **only 65 distinct implementations exist** — 228 packages are
byte-identical copies of three templates. because every clone could do every
sibling's job, a package's name told you nothing about what it contained.
`mem20adaptivepricingbrainz` contained no pricing brain.

so the groupings were decided deliberately, one at a time, and stored here as
data rather than left in a markdown table. this package makes package identity
**queryable**, so "which family does this belong to" has one answer rather than
as many as there are readers.

## what it does

| call | returns |
|---|---|
| `families()` | every family id |
| `purpose(f)` | what that family is for |
| `members(f)` | packages in that family |
| `family_of(pkg)` | the family a package belongs to, or `none` |
| `spec(pkg)` | family, name, purpose, what it must refuse, what proves it |
| `orphans()` | families with no members |
| `unmapped()` | packages with no family |
| `stats()` | integrity counters |

```bash
cd /opt/mem20/mem20famz
python3 -m mem20famz stats
python3 -m mem20famz which mem20adaptivepricingbrainz
python3 -m mem20famz spec  mem20adaptivepricingbrainz
```

## current state

**231 packages, 15 families, 0 unmapped, 0 orphans.** largest family 24
packages, smallest 4.

| family | packages | family | packages |
|---|---|---|---|
| simulation | 24 | markets-economics | 22 |
| production | 23 | compilation | 20 |
| networking | 19 | coordination | 15 |
| scheduling | 18 | human-team | 15 |
| learning-adaptation | 15 | interfaces | 14 |
| resilience | 12 | inference-serving | 11 |
| memory-cognition | 10 | trust-governance | 9 |
| platform | 4 | | |

## two things worth knowing about how it was built

**an earlier keyword pass was discarded.** scraping family keywords out of the
names left 161 of 231 packages unclassified, and the few that did match were
wrong. the stragglers here are assigned explicitly in `extra_assign` rather than
inferred, because inference is what produced the original problem.

**a test caught a real defect.** `test_two_clones_can_land_in_different_families`
failed on first run: `adaptivepricingbrainz` and `adaptiveforgettingenginez`
both landed in `learning-adaptation`, because the generic key `adaptive`
(8 characters) outscored `pricing` (7). that is precisely the failure this
registry exists to prevent — the whole point is that names discriminate. fixed
by dropping the over-broad key and assigning the ambiguous cases deliberately.

subsystems.description: Native mem20 OpenGame absorption — Game agents, environments, reward shaping, curriculum, multi-agent, replay
subsystems.name: mem20gamez
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20gamez

`mem20gamez` is mem20's native opengame-style reinforcement-learning package. it
contains executable torch agents, a deterministic in-package environment,
potential-based reward shaping, performance-gated curriculum, prioritized
replay, independent multi-agent dqn training, and an optional live http server.

no pretrained model, canned learning curve, random fallback environment, or
mock learning loop is used.

## verified capabilities

| area | implemented behavior |
|---|---|
| `environment.py` | `tinygridworld-v0` uses a fixed-size one-hot canvas, active-grid difficulty, deterministic movement, optional wind, wall/step penalties, and separate termination/truncation signals. `gymnasiumenvironment` is a strict optional wrapper; unknown environments fail instead of falling back to synthetic behavior. |
| `reward_shaper.py` | `potentialbasedshaper` implements `f = scale * (gamma * phi(s') - phi(s))`, forces terminal potential to zero, preserves the original reward, and rejects clipping that would break policy invariance. |
| `curriculum.py` | adaptive difficulty advances or regresses from measured grid progress. it acts once per complete performance window and clamps difficulty to configured bounds. the fixed observation canvas keeps replay and network shapes compatible across stages. |
| `replay_buffer.py` | a deterministic circular prioritized replay with exact-capacity eviction, proportional sampling, annealed importance weights, td-error priority updates, explicit exact-size batches, and shape-checked numpy outputs. |
| `agents.py` | double dqn with a target network, prioritized replay, optional dueling head, hard or polyak target synchronization, plus reinforce, clipped ppo, and discrete sac gradient implementations. |
| `trainer.py` | single-agent rollout/evaluation loops and interleaved multi-agent dqn. every multi-agent instance has its own environment, network, optimizer, target network, and replay buffer. |
| `cli.py` | training, evaluation, multi-agent training, checkpointing, subsystem checks, and an aiohttp server exposing `/health`, `/reset`, `/act`, `/step`, and `/learn`. |

the behavioral suite proves finite real gradient updates for reinforce, ppo, and
sac. the task-mastery learning assertion and the measured proof below use dqn,
which is the package's fully exercised short-run benchmark.

## measured dqn proof

command:

```bash
mem20gamez train \
  --agent dqn \
  --env tinygridworld-v0 \
  --grid-size 4 \
  --episodes 80 \
  --eval-episodes 20 \
  --batch-size 32 \
  --update-every 1 \
  --lr 0.01 \
  --gamma 0.99 \
  --shape \
  --seed 7
```

observed on the root venv with `torch 2.14.0+cpu`:

```text
before_mean_reward -9.730  before_success_rate 0.000
after_mean_reward   9.940  after_success_rate  1.000
first_window_reward 9.576  last_window_reward 9.928
first_window_loss   0.069549  last_window_loss 0.036290
elapsed=6.20 sec
```

those values come from the run itself. the agent learns the six-step optimal
route on the deterministic 4×4 grid: goal reward `10.0` plus six step penalties
`-0.01` equals `9.94`.

a separate two-agent 2×2 run moved each agent from mean reward `-9.91` to
`9.98`, with greedy success rate `1.00`, in `4.97 sec`.

a 40-episode curriculum run measured the expected 10-episode gates on the 4×4
canvas: difficulty `0.25`, `0.50`, `0.75`, then `1.00` at episodes 10, 20, 30,
and 40. runtime was `2.19 sec`.

## install

the runtime requires python 3.11+, numpy, torch, pyyaml, and aiohttp.

```bash
cd /opt/mem20/mem20gamez
python3 -m pip install -e .
python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

install gymnasium only when external gym environments are needed:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e ".[gym]"
```

`tinygridworld-v0` needs no external environment package.

## commands

```bash
# measured 4x4 dqn run
mem20gamez train --agent dqn --env tinygridworld-v0 --grid-size 4 \
  --episodes 80 --eval-episodes 20 --batch-size 32 --update-every 1 \
  --lr 0.01 --gamma 0.99 --shape --seed 7

# save a trained dqn checkpoint
mem20gamez train --agent dqn --shape --checkpoint /tmp/mem20gamez-dqn.pt

# independent, interleaved dqn agents
mem20gamez multi --agents 2 --grid-size 2 --episodes 35 \
  --batch-size 8 --update-every 1 --lr 0.02 --gamma 0.95 --shape --seed 31

# live dqn process
mem20gamez serve --env tinygridworld-v0 --agent dqn --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8007

# fast subsystem contract check
mem20gamez test
```

the packaged server is persisted as `mem20gamez.service`, enabled and started
with systemd, so it survives reboot rather than running as a floating process.

## verification

```bash
cd /opt/mem20/mem20gamez
python3 -m pytest -q
python3 -m ruff check .
```

current result: `29 passed`, and ruff reports `all checks passed!`.

## managed members (package-review integration)

single-purpose game organs grouped here by reference; they live in their
own top-level directories and are smoke-verified there:

- `mem20ailevelarchitectz`
- `mem20alternativedatabaseplaygroundz`
- `mem20dynamicquestrewardcomposerz`
- `mem20gameproductioncontrolcenterz`
- `mem20simz`

subsystems.description: Real local Google ADK-style agents, tools, runners, sessions, memory, flows, and serving
subsystems.name: mem20googlez
subsystems.readme_text:
# mem20googlez

`mem20googlez` is a native, local google adk-style runtime. it provides agents,
executable tools, a real assistant/tool/result loop, persistent sessions,
file-backed memory, sequential flows, and a fastapi service.

production model calls are http calls to a local endpoint. the default resolver
checks ollama first and uses the openai-compatible mem20/litellm gateway on port
4000 when ollama is unavailable. no model download or paid api is required.

## install

```bash
cd /opt/mem20/mem20googlez
python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

the package console command is `mem20googlez`.

## local model

the default local model is `qwen2.5-coder:0.5b` at `http://127.0.0.1:11434`.
check the endpoint and the installed model with:

```bash
mem20googlez health
mem20googlez run --provider ollama --agent chat --input "reply with the word ready."
```

configuration can be supplied with `--config`, `mem20googlez_config`, or
`mem20googlez_*` environment variables. the important settings are
`mem20googlez_ollama_url`, `mem20googlez_gateway_url`,
`mem20googlez_default_model`, `mem20googlez_session_db`, and
`mem20googlez_memory_dir`.

## library use

```python
import asyncio

from mem20googlez import durablerunner, llmagent, function_tool


@function_tool
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b


async def main():
    agent = llmagent(
        name="calculator",
        instruction="use add for arithmetic, then state the result.",
        tools=[add],
    )
    runner = durablerunner(agent, app_name="demo")
    result = await runner.run("user-1", input="what is 7 plus 9?")
    print(result.final_output)


asyncio.run(main())
```

`durablerunner` uses sqlite for sessions and json files for memory. a new
runner with the same configuration can load the same conversation after a
process restart. `inmemoryrunner` is an explicitly ephemeral library helper and
is not used by the production cli or service.

## flows

```python
import asyncio

from mem20googlez import flow, llmagent

plan = llmagent(name="plan", instruction="create a short implementation plan.")
review = llmagent(name="review", instruction="review the plan and mark it done.")
flow = flow("plan-review", [plan, review])
result = asyncio.run(flow.run("build a persistent memory service"))
print(result.final_output)
```

the output of each agent is the input to the next agent. passing a durable
runner or session and memory services to `flow` persists every step.

## http service

```bash
mem20googlez serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002
```

endpoints:

| method | path | purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| get | `/health` | resolve the real provider and check its health |
| get | `/` | service, storage, agents, and endpoint information |
| get | `/agents` | list registered agents and executable tools |
| post | `/agents/{name}/run` | run an agent with `{"input":"...", "user_id":"...", "session_id":"..."}` |
| get | `/sessions` | list persisted sessions; optional `app_name` and `user_id` filters |
| get | `/sessions/{id}` | read a persisted session and all events |

example:

```bash
curl -ss http://127.0.0.1:8002/health
curl -ss http://127.0.0.1:8002/agents
curl -ss http://127.0.0.1:8002/agents/chat/run \
  -h 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"reply with the number 42.","user_id":"curl"}'
```

the service unit is `mem20googlez-serve.service`. it runs the installed
`mem20googlez serve` command under systemd; after installation:

```bash
systemctl status mem20googlez-serve.service
systemctl is-active mem20googlez-serve.service
```

## tests

the hermetic suite injects a deterministic in-process provider into the same
runner and asgi application code. that provider exists only in the test module
and is not imported by production modules. the production path always resolves
an http provider unless a caller explicitly injects a provider object.

```bash
cd /opt/mem20/mem20googlez
python3 -m pytest -q
```

the suite covers executable tools, the assistant/tool/final-answer loop,
cross-runner sqlite session persistence, file memory persistence, a-to-b flows,
and the http endpoints. a real local-endpoint smoke test can be run explicitly:

```bash
mem20googlez_real_tests=1 python3 -m pytest -q -m real
```

# mem20instantappsynthesisz — instant app synthesis (rm-010, #327)

**outcome:** compile a plain-language objective into a working composition of existing freestack capabilities.
**breakthrough:** users describe an outcome and receive a usable app in minutes.

preserves legacy domain api (**#318 peer dependency**) and capability engine/cli/10-scenario simulator (`compose` operation kind).

## legacy domain api (preserved for #318)
`synthesize(spec)`, `scaffold(app)`, `estimate_size(app)`, `validate_spec(spec)`, `deploy_config(app,target="vercel")`.

## meaningful cross-subsystem wiring (criterion 6)
| peer | real calls | synthesis role (feeds composition outcome) |
|---|---|---|
| `mem20deterministicconfigurationgraphz` | `add_node`,`add_edge`,`resolve` | app/page config graph resolution |
| `mem20semanticobjectgraphz` | `canonical`,`stable_hash`,`words` | spec/component semantic identity |
| `mem20pipez` | `version_asset`,`vc_health` | synthesized artifact versioning |
| `mem20dynamicskillgraphz` | `add_skill`,`learning_path` | capability composition path |
| `mem20relationshipcontextgraphz` | `canonical`,`similarity` | objective-to-composition intent context |
| `mem20capabilitygapmapperz` | `canonical`,`stable_hash` | capability gap/coverage check |

## runnable example (verified)
```bash
cd /opt/mem20
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20instantappsynthesisz simulate
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20instantappsynthesisz execute '{"objective":"build a todo app","spec":{"name":"todo","pages":["home"],"components":["list","form"]}}'
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m mem20instantappsynthesisz serve --port 8807
```

## tests / conformance
```bash
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python -m pytest mem20instantappsynthesisz/tests mem20instantappsynthesisz/mem20instantappsynthesisz/tests -q --noconftest
pythonpath=/opt/mem20 .venv/bin/python scripts/renovation/conformance.py mem20instantappsynthesisz
```

subsystems.readme_text:
# rm-184 — intent-to-agent matchmaker

**owner:** ariel  
**lane:** mission dispatch, execution visibility, and real-time operations

## outcome
match user requests to capable agents and tool combinations

## breakthrough
users do not need to know which runtime or model performs the work

this package implements the locally executable/non-human portion of this off record lab roadmap on a shared, zero-dependency runtime substrate. it includes typed/versioned roadmap validation, sqlite wal state + event history, resumable/idempotent jobs, cancellation/timeouts/quotas, deterministic recovery, adaptive mode decisions with confidence/alternatives/bottlenecks/explanations, feedback tuning, cli + typed client + http api + browser command surface + event stream, local/hybrid/cloud peer execution, conflict-safe lww synchronization, caching, backpressure/failover, metrics, simulator scenarios, benchmark tooling, safety gating, and a rollback manifest.

the domain engine for this package is keyed specifically to rm-184 and produces deterministic executable results for the roadmap's core operation using only local standard-library code. external hardware, proprietary models, production credentials, live third-party services, and deployment authorization are intentionally not fabricated; those remain environment-bound integration points.

## run
```bash
python run.py inspect
python run.py run '{"text":"demo","cache":false}'
python run.py simulate
python run.py benchmark --runs 5
python run.py serve --port 8765
```

open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` for the live command surface.
